Free Trade Agreement between New Zealand and the People's Republic of China

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (Public Act 2009 No 35, as amended by the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Amendment Acts 2015 and 2017); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (Definitions) Regulations 2018 (LI 2018/74); Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105, as amended by the Companies Amendment Act 2023 introducing the beneficial ownership register administered by the Registrar of Companies); Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (Public Act 2013 No 69).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the New Zealand company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the destination or origin state is an Apostille Convention state: notarize if required, then obtain a single Hague Apostille from the competent authority in the issuing state; never add consular legalization. If the state is not an Apostille party: notarize and then use consular legalization at the New Zealand Embassy or High Commission with jurisdiction; never use an Apostille. The two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: obtain an official certified copy from Companies Office, then obtain an Apostille from the designated New Zealand competent authority. Non-Apostille route: notarize the Companies Office certificate and present it to the New Zealand consular post for legalization. Do not perform both processes sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the ultimate parent entity, notarized by a notary public in the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a parent jurisdiction that is an Apostille party: notarize the resolution/power of attorney, obtain an Apostille from that jurisdiction's competent authority, and present to the New Zealand registrar or bank. For a non-Apostille parent jurisdiction: notarize, then submit to the New Zealand Embassy or High Commission for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, never cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board and initial shareholders of the New Zealand company, registered by the New Zealand Companies Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If using the New Zealand-origin document abroad in an Apostille state: have the constitution notarized as a true copy and apostilled by the New Zealand competent authority. If the receiving state is not an Apostille party: notarize and legalize by the New Zealand consulate. No state may receive both an Apostille and a consular legalizing stamp.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank holding the ultimate beneficial owner's or parent entity's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The original bank letter must be notarized by the issuing bank or its counsel. If the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille party, attach a Hague Apostille; if it is not, the letter must be consular legalized by the New Zealand Embassy or High Commission in that jurisdiction. The bank letter is ineffective if both an Apostille and consular legalization are attached.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, all directors, UBOs at the 25% threshold, authorized signatories, senior executives, and counterparties of the global EOR/payroll branch must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the UK OFSI consolidated sanctions list, and New Zealand's domestic sanctions measures administered by the Police Financial Intelligence Unit, FMA, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and local AML/CFT supervisors. PEP screening must cover direct PEPs, immediate family members, known close associates, and any negative adverse-media record. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any PEP or sanctioned-country nexus, including source of wealth verification, independent audit of beneficial ownership

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), particularly ss 10-16, 21-22, 26-40, 119, 122, 124, 126-128, 157-164 and 189-200; Companies (Fees) Regulations 2016; Labour Hire Licensing Act 2020, ss 8-15 and 24-30.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, an operating arm of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic Application for Registration of a Company submitted through the New Zealand Companies Register online portal, together with the Company Constitution, shareholder subscription statement, and signed consents to act as directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up capital and no statutory escrow or blocked deposit requirement. Under the Companies Act 1993, shares may be issued for consideration determined by the board, but any share subscription consideration must be paid or satisfied in accordance with section 38 of the Act. The company may be incorporated with one or more shares of any nominal value, and non-resident ownership is permitted.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME], a limited company governed by the Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand). The first meeting of the Board of Directors (the 'Board') of [Company Name] (the 'Company') was duly convened and held on [date] at [time] at the registered office of the Company. Present in person and by unanimous resolution were the undersigned directors, namely [Director A] and [Director B]. The Chair confirmed that a quorum was present and that the meeting had been validly called in accordance with the constitution and the applicable provisions of the Companies Act 1993. The Board had before it the application for incorporation, the proposed constitution, the consents to act as directors and shareholders, the certificate of incorporation when issued, and the banking mandate schedules. The following resolutions were duly proposed, seconded and unanimously passed. 1. ADOPTION OF CONSTITUTION: That the constitution submitted to the Registrar shall be adopted without modification as the constitution of the Company, effective on registration, and that a certified copy shall be placed in the Company's statutory records. 2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: That the authorised share capital of the Company shall be [number] ordinary shares of NZ$[amount] each, and that the subscribers named in the incorporation application and described in the confidential share subscription schedule shall subscribe for such shares at the consideration set against the schedule, such consideration to be equivalent to fair value and to be paid or satisfied in accordance with section 38 of the Companies Act 1993. The Board is hereby authorised to allot the subscribed shares, to issue corresponding share certificates, and to record transfers thereafter only with board approval where the constitution so requires. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: That the registered office of the Company shall be [physical address in New Zealand], which address is a physical place, not a postal office box, and that the Company shall maintain at that address the share register, director register, constitution, minutes and other statutory records required by the Companies Act 1993. 4. BANKING AUTHORISATION: That the Company shall open operating and payroll bank accounts at [bank name] in New Zealand and on the Wise international payment infrastructure for global contractor payments. The authorised signatories shall be [Director A], [Director B] and [Finance Officer]. All cheques, electronic funds transfers, payment instructions, loan or guarantee instruments, and banking mandates shall be signed by any two of the three authorised signatories, provided that any single signatory may execute transactions up to NZ$[single signatory limit] and any two signatories may execute unlimited transactions. The bank is authorised to rely conclusively on these signatories until the Company delivers a superseding resolution. 5. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: That [Director A] be and is hereby appointed Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director, and [Director B] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary and Compliance Officer. Each appointee consents to act and shall hold office until resignation, removal, death, or disqualification under the Companies Act 1993. The Managing Director shall be responsible for Global Employer of Record payroll operations and client contracting. The Compliance Officer shall be responsible for maintaining statutory records and submitting annual returns. 6. LICENSING AND GOVERNANCE: That management promptly apply for a Labour Hire Licence under the Labour Hire Licensing Act 2020, register with Inland Revenue as an employer for PAYE and goods and services tax as applicable, register with the Accident Compensation Corporation, and implement employment compliance policies to ensure the Company does not knowingly engage in a breach of New Zealand employment or immigration law. FURTHER RESOLVED that any one director be and is hereby authorised and directed to execute, file, and deliver all documents, notices, statutory declarations and applications, and to engage professional legal, tax and corporate service advisers as necessary to implement these resolutions. All actions taken pursuant to these resolutions shall be final and binding upon the Company. DATED this [date] at [place]. [Signature] Chairman; [Signature] Director.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Reservation via the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Register, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) - online portal at www.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Register using a RealMe authenticated account and run a name search on the proposed company name, including the restricted suffix "Limited" or "Ltd". Verify that the desired name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or a name already reserved under section 22 of the Companies Act 1993. Submit the online name reservation application and pay the prescribed fee by debit or credit card. The reservation is valid for 20 business days and secures priority for the proposed corporate name before incorporation. If the name contains a restricted word, supply a statement of grounds and supporting evidence to the Registrar for approval. Record the reservation number and all alternative names for use in the incorporation application and internal compliance checklists.
required_dossiers: RealMe login credentials for each applicant or authorised agent
Proposed company name and two alternative names
Name reservation application form generated online
Statement of grounds if any restricted word is proposed
Applicant identity verification documents
Contact email and physical address of applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or treated as confusingly similar, the applicant will receive written reasons from the Companies Office. File a new reservation using one of the alternative names, or apply to the Registrar for consent to a restricted word. A suspended reservation can be corrected within 10 working days before expiry; otherwise the fee is lost and a fresh application is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitution and Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Proposed directors, subscribers and their New Zealand corporate legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution in accordance with the Companies Act 1993, or elect to rely on the default rules in Schedule 1 if no bespoke constitution is adopted. For a Global Employer of Record platform, a bespoke constitution is strongly recommended to address risk management, share transfer, director indemnity, and unanimous shareholder approval provisions. Obtain physical or electronic signatures from each subscriber on the subscription deed, from each proposed director on the consent to act as director, and from each shareholders on the constitution where required. Verify proof of identity and residential address for every director and ensure at least one director is ordinarily resident in New Zealand or resident in Australia under the reciprocal Australian director exemption. Notarisation is not universally required for electronic registration, but documents signed outside New Zealand should be notarised or certified by a Notary Public if the Registrar or bank requests high-identity assurance. Retain wet signed original documents in the corporate records binder and scan all documents for online attachment.
required_dossiers: Bespoke Company Constitution or written election to use Companies Act 1993 default rules
Share subscription and capital contribution deed for each subscriber
Consent to act as director signed by each proposed director
Passport or national identity card of each director and subscriber
Proof of residential address for each director (utility bill or bank statement)
Certified English translation of any non-English corporate or identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries a signature or consent form, the applicant should file a fresh corrected consent with the same effective date and a letter of explanation. Incorrect documents may be withdrawn and replaced online through the revision function before the incorporation application is approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Application to the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) - online Companies Register portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name reservation is granted, complete the online 'Register Company' application in the Companies Register portal. Enter the reserved company name, proposed registered office physical address, principal place of business, director details and shareholder details, initial share allotment and share class details. Upload the signed constitution, consents to act, subscription records and any certified translations. Confirm that the registered office is a physical New Zealand address and not a post office box. Pay the incorporation fee using a debit or credit card. The Companies Office then performs verifications under sections 12 to 16 and 21 to 22 of the Companies Act 1993, checking director residence, disqualification, and name availability. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the certificate of incorporation with a company number, and the company acquires separate legal personality. Download the certificate of incorporation and the confirmation of company details from the portal; no physical certificate is couriered by default.
required_dossiers: Valid name reservation number and reserved company name
Completed online registration application form
Adopted Company Constitution
Signed consent to act as director for every director
Share subscription schedule and initial share allotment record
Director and shareholder identification documents
Registered office physical address and landlord or agent consent where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or placed on hold, the Companies Office issues a specific query in the 'My Companies' dashboard. The applicant should respond and resubmit corrected information within 15 working days. Where the name reservation has expired, the applicant must reserve a new name and file the application again. Judicial review is not available until registration remedies are exhausted, so the practical cure is immediate resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Registered Office and Establishment of Statutory Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and the company's appointed registered agent or corporate services provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the company is incorporated, verify that the registered office filed on the Companies Register is a physical location in New Zealand that the company is legally authorised to use. If the registered office is provided by a corporate agent, execute a service agreement and file the agent's address for service. Open the statutory minute book containing the certificate of incorporation, constitution, directors register, shareholders register, share certificates and all board and shareholder minutes. Under sections 87 to 92 of the Companies Act 1993, the company must keep proper accounting records that correctly record the transactions and financial position of the company. Ensure the share register and director register are maintained at the registered office, and file any future change of registered office within 10 working days after the change is made. This step establishes the governance spine required to support the Labour Hire Licence application and banking due diligence.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and company number
Registered office service agreement with agent
Statutory minute book and corporate records binder
Directors register and shareholders register templates
Consents to act as directors and subscribed share register
Copy of the adopted Constitution
Board resolution appointing registered agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office is rejected for being non-physical or unauthorised, file a replacement physical address immediately and present landlord or agent consent. Late filing penalties may apply under the Companies Act 1993, but the Registrar allows an immediate cured filing through the online portal without court intervention.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Financial Mandate Activation for Payroll Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorised New Zealand bank (such as ANZ, ASB, BNZ or Westpac) and the New Zealand Companies Office for corporate verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the certificate of incorporation, adopted constitution, board resolution, and Companies Register excerpt to the chosen bank. Complete the corporate customer due diligence form, identifying the beneficial owners, directors, and company business purpose. Provide proof of registered office and evidence of directors' residential addresses. Deliver the certified board resolution authorising the account opening and prescribing the authorised signatories and transactional limits. For a Global Employer of Record company with cross-border contractor payroll, request the bank to enable local payroll direct debit facilities and integrate the Wise multi-currency payment rail. The bank will run sanctions, anti-money-laundering, and adverse media checks on the company and its directors. Once the account is live, connect the payment rails to the in-house payroll ledger, record the bank mandate in the statutory minute book, and issue a payment authorisation matrix. Full activation typically occurs within five working days after the bank receives clean due diligence material.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and company number
Adopted company constitution
Certified copy of the first board resolution
Companies Register extract confirming directors
Identification documents for all directors and signatories
Proof of residential address for each director
Beneficial ownership declaration form
Payroll processing description and client contract sample for EOR operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further information, provide a source-of-funds declaration, an aggregator organisational chart, and audited or management accounts where available. If the application is suspended pending internal review, the company may escalate the matter to the bank's commercial dispute resolution team and provide supplementary evidence of lawful staffing and employment practices. The Labour Hire Licence may also be used as evidence of regulatory standing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Labour Hire Licence Application and Tax, ACC and PAYE Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Labour Inspectorate of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); Inland Revenue; Accident Compensation Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: A Global Employer of Record and cross-border contractor staffing agency that places workers with host businesses is a labour hire company under the Labour Hire Licensing Act 2020 and must obtain a Labour Hire Licence before operating lawfully. Prepare the Labour Hire Licence application online, including the certificate of incorporation, constitution, and declarations that the company and its officers are not disqualified or prohibited persons. Provide evidence of robust employment standards compliance, payroll administration capacity, immigration due diligence, and an accident and injury management plan. Pay the application fee and submit the application to the Labour Inspectorate. The Inspectorate may request police clearance for officers and details of all hosts and workers deployed. Simultaneously register with Inland Revenue as an employer for PAYE and as a GST registrant if annual taxable supplies will exceed NZ$60,000. Register with ACC for employer injury cover and maintain a workplace health and safety policy under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. Upon approval, display the licence at the principal place of business and on the company website, and renew annually.
required_dossiers: Labour Hire Licence application form
Certificate of incorporation and Companies Register search
Constitution and first board resolution pack
Declarations of no disqualification for directors and senior managers
Police certificate or expected police vetting for each director
Payroll system description and employment agreements template
Host client engagement agreements and worker assignment records
Inland Revenue employer registration confirmation
ACC employer registration certificate
Workplace health and safety policy and incident reporting procedure
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Labour Inspectorate issues a notice of query, the licensee must answer in writing within the stated period, typically 10 working days, and provide any missing declarations or supporting records. If a licence is refused, the company may apply to the District Court for review under section 48 of the Labour Hire Licensing Act 2020, and the Labour Inspectorate may at its discretion issue a transitional licence while remedial conditions are implemented.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Labour Inspectorate of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); Inland Revenue; Accident Compensation Corporation; and, for any future physical premises, the relevant territorial authority under the Building Act 2004 and Fire and Emergency New Zealand.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Labour Hire Licence required under the Labour Hire Licensing Act 2020, plus Inland Revenue PAYE employer registration and ACC employer registration for a Global Employer of Record/Staffing Agency.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority New Zealand (for national environmental standards) and the relevant regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category Not Applicable for a pure digital/consulting Global Employer of Record and cross-border contractor payroll platform. No physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing activity is carried out under ISIC 7810, so no public or notified Environmental Impact Assessment, no resource consent, and no discharge permit is required. If the company later unlocks a physical warehouse or light industrial facility, a classification under the Resource Management Act 1991 would be required before commencement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for current office-based EOR operations: zero process wastewater, zero volatile organic compound emissions, zero point-source air discharge, zero hazardous waste inventory. Office e-waste must be disposed of in accordance with the Waste Minimisation Act 2008. If a physical premises is later occupied, the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality 2004 would apply, including the 24-hour average PM10 concentration limit of 50 micrograms per cubic metre, and all trade wastewater would require regional council consent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a pure digital/consulting Global Employer of Record platform because there is no physical production, chemical plant, assembly line, or warehousing operation. However, if the company later leases or occupies an office, it must comply with the Building Act 2004 Building Warrant of Fitness regime, maintain an approved means-of-escape and fire evacuation scheme with Fire and Emergency New Zealand, and carry out workplace health and safety assessments under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. For current off-premises consulting operations, no physical civil defence fire certificate or structural load inspection is mandated.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), trading as Te Tari Taake; online filing and compliance portal is myIR
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a New Zealand registered limited company, the IRD number (tax file number) is issued automatically upon incorporation with the Companies Office; if a foreign non-resident entity does not have a NZ company, it must complete the Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application (IR742) via myIR or by mail to the Inland Revenue Department, providing proof of foreign incorporation, director particulars, and appointment of a New Zealand tax agent or a physical address for service.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 gross taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance or electronic invoicing; e-invoicing is voluntary on the PEPPOL network; GST returns are filed and paid electronically via myIR; there is no continuous transaction control or anti-fraud digital stamping regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1986 to goods physically exported by the supplier within 28 days, and to services, including employer-of-record and labour staffing services, supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of performance, provided the services are not performed for a New Zealand resident and do not relate directly to land in New Zealand or to other excluded domestic assets.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where export zero-rating is claimed without substantiation, Inland Revenue may issue a retrospective assessment for GST together with shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for an acceptable interpretation, 40% for gross carelessness, and 100% for evasion or fraud, plus late payment penalties and use-of-money interest. Criminal prosecution is possible under TAA sections 143 and 148 for knowingly providing false information or deliberately evading assessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates an open and fully convertible currency regime; the NZD is freely floating with no foreign-exchange controls administered by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand. Both current and capital account transactions are unrestricted. A New Zealand entity may raise inbound equity, maintain foreign-currency accounts, and remit dividends, royalties, or service fees without routine exchange-control approval. Banks conduct resident bank transaction reporting for statistical purposes only and perform standard AML/CFT checks. There are no surrender requirements on export proceeds or inward remittances. For an EOR staffing agency, contractor payroll outflows and client invoicing in foreign currencies may be settled directly in the selected currency or converted to NZD at commercial dealing rates. The only material friction is documentation: a bank must be satisfied as to the source of funds and the underlying commercial substance of each cross-border flow to discharge obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is permitted, subject to solvency and tax compliance such as resident withholding tax on dividends. Because the jurisdiction does not impose investment licences or exchange-control barriers, the treasury design should focus on bank onboarding, counterparty due diligence, and clean clearing rails rather than regulatory approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. New Zealand imposes no statutory surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion period, and no required ratio for export foreign currency receipts. Exporters and service providers may retain, borrow, or convert such proceeds at their discretion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account with Multi-Currency Facility
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditionally viable as a supplementary rail, not a primary banking substitute. New Zealand has no dedicated EMI licensing regime. An offshore digital EMI may not operate as a bank or accept deposits unless licensed under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand framework and registered on the Financial Service Providers Register. However, registered money remitters and payment facilities can deliver cross-border contractor payouts. Wise is commonly used for low-value payroll disbursements, but for a global EOR with material throughput the treasury should maintain primary balances in NZ tier-1 banks and use an EMI only for small-value, non-critical payments after confirming the EMI's FSP registration, AML/CFT supervision, and trust account segregation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate exists requiring directors to appear physically in-branch. New Zealand AML/CFT allows identity verification through electronic systems, provided the verification methods meet customer due diligence standards. In practice, major banks require one director or authorised signatory to open the corporate and foreign-currency accounts, either in-person at a branch or through a remote video interview supported by certified passport copies and bank-issued digital signing. Remote opening is normally available for non-resident directors if the company has a registered office in New Zealand and an engaged external accountant. Consular proxy opening is occasionally accepted but is not a statutory right and depends on the bank's internal policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity across non-resident shareholders or discretionary trust investors, creating an inability to identify the ultimate owner and source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passports, a current New Zealand Companies Office extract showing directors and share allotments, a signed statutory declaration from each ultimate beneficial owner, trust deed or corporate ownership chart, foreign registry certificates for any intermediate corporate entities, and an independent legal opinion confirming the control chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border payments to contractors in multiple jurisdictions inconsistent with the declared employer-of-record business model and creating concerns about round-tripping or unlicensed remittance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed global EOR service agreements with end clients, contractor employment agreements, monthly payroll registers, contractor invoices and time sheets, IRD/PAYE monthly filings, evidence of payroll tax payments, and a transaction-level reconciliation between client funding receipts and contractor disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from crypto exchanges, third-party lending platforms, or unidentifiable inward remittances, raising source-of-funds red flags during capital escrow account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements from the shareholder's operating account, signed shareholder loan or equity subscription agreements, board resolutions authorising the share issuance, notarised source-of-wealth statements, audited financial statements or accountant letters, and an explicit declaration that no crypto or gambling proceeds are used for treasury balances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, anti-bribery, or politically exposed person exposure arising from the contractor geography and cross-border payroll beneficiary population.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A documented sanctions screening policy and screening results for all contractors and ultimate payees, contractor HR dossiers containing nationality, residence, passport, and work permits, standard EOR agreements with global compliance clauses, local legal opinions covering employment and immigration law in each contractor jurisdiction, and a quarterly refresh of the bank's enhanced due diligence pack.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity into a New Zealand limited company requires no pre-approval, but bank compliance expects the payment narrative to state 'Shareholder Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Injection'. The transfer should be routed as a SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's own account to the company settlement account at a licensed New Zealand bank and must not be sourced from commingled third-party funds. Where funds arrive in foreign currency, the bank either converts to NZD at the dealing rate or credits a designated multi-currency account. For capital verification, the company must retain the SWIFT reference, a board resolution authorising the share allotment, the shareholder's source-of-funds documentation, an updated share register, an allotment return filed with the New Zealand Companies Office, and an auditor or chartered accountant confirmation of the cleared funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Local New Zealand contractor payroll is cleared via domestic payroll direct credit through the incumbent bank using NZD same-day clearing. Cross-border contractor payments are best executed via SWIFT MT103 to the contractor's local bank account, using the bank's payment purpose code for payroll or professional services. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are not appropriate for payroll disbursements and should be reserved for physical goods or trade finance assets. For recurring EOR payroll runs, the treasury should set up batch payment templates, retain full beneficiary banking details, and use the primary bank's foreign-currency dealing desk rather than an EMI for any payment above commercial materiality thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla forward foreign-exchange contracts for NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/AUD and other G10 currency pairs backed by underlying payroll or invoicing exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for deliverability-constrained emerging-market currencies used only where onshore local forwards are unavailable
Cross-currency swaps for longer-duration operational liquidity or intercompany loan positions
Plain vanilla FX options with zero speculative premium, restricted to hedging confirmed contractor payroll and client fee exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return on Companies Register (confirmation of registered office, directors, shareholders, principal activity, and company status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due each year on the company's Companies Office filing balance date, generally the anniversary month of incorporation; file within 28 days after the due date and not more than 1 month before the balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee NZD 200; continued non-compliance triggers a Registrar warning and administrative strike-off from the Register; restoration after strike-off requires court or Registrar approval plus additional fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return and terminal tax reconciliation (IR4) for the NZ tax year ended 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standard 31 March balance date: IR4 return due by 7 July following balance date for online non-agent filers; tax agents may receive extension under IRD Extension of Time arrangements; terminal tax due following balance date as specified by IRD, commonly 7 February for tax-agent cases and 7 May for non-agent filers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Use-of-money interest on underpaid or terminal tax; late payment penalty of 1% of unpaid tax on the first day of default and 4% after day 7; late filing penalty up to NZD 500, or up to NZD 4,000 for certain offshore or avoidance-related failures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and independent audit report (if the company is large or an audit is shareholder-mandated)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; where trigger applies, Registrar of Companies and Inland Revenue as supporting filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements to be prepared within 5 months after balance date; if audited, audit opinion to be completed before the earlier of company return filing or financial statements delivery deadline; filing with Companies Office, if mandatory, occurs with the annual return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be subject to infringement notices up to NZD 10,000; failure to deliver financial statements or audit report may result in Companies Office enforcement action, director personal liability, and potential disclosure of default in public register records.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered when the company is an FMC reporting entity or qualifies as large under Companies Act 1993 s 45(2) (meets any one of: total assets NZD 60 million+, total revenue NZD 30 million+, or 50+ full-time equivalent employees); a shareholder with 10% or more of voting rights may also compel an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: For-profit entity applying New Zealand Generally Accepted Accounting Practice (NZ GAAP) issued by the External Reporting Board (XRB); large and FMC reporting entities apply NZ IFRS or NZ IFRS RDR, and small or medium entities may use simplified Tier 3 or Tier 4 accounting standards; statutory accounts also comply with Companies Act 1993 and Financial Reporting Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate public UBO registry; the annual return confirms the registered shareholding, directors, ultimate share allocation, and company details. Share transfers and Board changes must be notified to the Companies Register by event-driven notice before they can be relied on against third parties; in the annual confirmation the directors must verify that the register section reflects all share transfers made during the year. If the entity is an AML/CFT reporting entity, current beneficial ownership records must be obtained, verified, and retained, and the annual compliance report must identify any material control gaps.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 1,200 annual typical market range for professional registered office and company secretarial support in New Zealand.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 30,000 typical for a mid-sized EOR or payroll services entity if audit is required or contracted; below mandatory thresholds no audit fee is necessary.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday or concessional regime applies to a New Zealand resident company. A refundable Research and Development Tax Credit of 15% is available on eligible R&D expenditure under Income Tax Act 2007, s LYB 1AB. For an EOR/staffing agency, ordinary deductions are available for payroll costs, subcontracted contractor payments, platform software, rent, insurance, and administrative overheads. New Zealand operates an imputation system; resident shareholders receiving imputed dividends obtain a credit for the 28% company tax paid.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 – Income Tax Return for Companies; mandatory electronic filing through the New Zealand Inland Revenue (Te Tari Taake) 'myIR' online portal; paper IR4 remains available only in exceptional circumstances and for certain non-resident filings.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July following the balance date (Tax Administration Act 1994, s 37). Terminal tax on the assessed income is due by 7 February. A tax agent holding a valid extension of time may defer filing to 31 March of the following year, which correspondingly moves the terminal tax due date to 7 April.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All income derived in the income year, including gross revenue from global EOR payroll services, contractor placement fees, employer-of-record margin, and any foreign-source income of the New Zealand resident company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A resident New Zealand company is taxable on worldwide income; the return must include all overseas-derived amounts subject to New Zealand tax, with foreign tax credit claims recorded separately. Nondeductible items and capital amounts must be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable business deductions including salaries and wages paid to seconded employees, subcontracted contractor costs, global payroll platform fees, IT/software subscriptions, legal and accounting fees, office rent, insurance, and other expenditure necessarily incurred in gaining assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses with a sufficient nexus to New Zealand-assessable income are deductible. Capital expenditure, penalties, fines, and payments that would constitute tax avoidance or dividend recharacterisation are denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3A - Net Taxable Income or Loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed as total income less allowable deductions. If a loss arises, it is carried forward subject to the 49% shareholder continuity requirement and may be offset against future profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A loss must be supported by contemporaneous financial statements; non-resident shareholding changes in excess of the continuity threshold extinguish the loss carry-forward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax liability calculated at the 28% corporate rate on net taxable income, per Income Tax Act 2007, Schedule 1, Part A.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The rate is a flat final entity-level rate; no branch or special diverted income rate applies to a standard NZ Ltd. Retained profits remain taxed at 28%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits claimed against the tax liability: resident withholding tax (RWT), provisional tax paid, foreign tax credits, imputation credits, and the 15% R&D tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits must be substantiated by withholding certificates, tax receipts, or IRD approvals. Excessive or unsupported credits trigger use-of-money interest and shortfall penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6A - Terminal Tax Due or Refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The residual balance after deducting tax credits from the annual tax liability; if positive, terminal tax is payable; if negative, a refund is due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Terminal tax on a standard balance date is due 7 February; the 'held-over' terminal tax date with a tax agent extension is 7 April. Refunds are paid into the company's New Zealand bank account.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the 49% shareholder continuity required for loss carry-forward and imputation credit account balance carry-forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Changes in non-resident ownership must be disclosed; failure to maintain continuity invalidates prior losses and imputation credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual reconciliation of imputation credits: opening balance, credits attached to dividends paid, and closing balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imputation credits attached to dividends reduce or eliminate NZ resident shareholder tax; for non-residents, fully imputed dividends reduce NRWT exposure under certain DTA provisions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: initial NZD 50 penalty, rising by NZD 100 per month of continued non-filing, capped at NZD 1,000. An increased late filing penalty of up to NZD 500 and criminal prosecution may apply to promoters and persistent offenders. Late payment penalties: 1% immediately on the due date, 4% after seven days, then 1% per month. Use-of-money interest accrues daily on any unpaid tax at the prescribed IRD rate (currently approximately 8–10%). Shortfall penalties (20% to 150%) apply separately on any understatement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provisional Tax Instalments – managed through the myIR portal and calculated on the basis of the prior year's residual income tax; no standalone paper return is required for the instalment system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a 31 March balance date, the three provisional tax instalments are due on 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May of the relevant income year, with a terminal balancing payment on 7 February. The standard uplift for a continuing business is the prior year's residual income tax plus 5%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the estimation method: standard uplift (prior-year residual tax plus 5%), ratio method, or a reasonable estimate of current-year liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The estimate for a company whose parent is offshore must incorporate arm's-length transfer pricing outcomes; deliberate underestimation of EOR profits is a shortfall penalty trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the projected residual income tax across the three instalment dates using prescribed percentages.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The instalment calculations must be converted to NZD; payments made from foreign bank accounts must clear on or before the statutory due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of payment amounts allocated to each instalment date and reconciliation against the corresponding IR4 assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Underpayment gives rise to early-payment penalties and use-of-money interest from the original due date of each instalment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Insufficient provisional tax: use-of-money interest on the shortfall; late payment penalties of 1% immediately, 4% after 7 days, and 1% monthly. Where an estimate is made without reasonable care, a shortfall penalty of 20% may be imposed, rising to 100% for an abusive position and 150% for evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) is charged at 30% on dividends paid by a New Zealand company to non-resident shareholders. To obtain a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must provide: (i) an up-to-date Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the home-jurisdiction tax authority; (ii) a written declaration of treaty residence and beneficial ownership; and (iii) completion and submission of the Inland Revenue declaration form for reduced NRWT rates (commonly referenced as IR 3155 or the DTA rate application). The New Zealand paying company must hold the certificate and declaration on or before the dividend payment date; otherwise, it must withhold at the 30% domestic rate. Reduced rates under the Australia–NZ DTA can be 15% for portfolio shareholders and 5% for substantial Australian corporate holders; most other NZ DTAs cap dividends at 15%. The IRD may issue an annual reduced-rate approval through myIR to support continuous withholding patterns.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT: 15% on royalties and 15% on interest. An Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may apply to interest paid to non-residents by an approved issuer, replacing NRWT for qualifying registered financial arrangements. Treaty rates vary: royalties are commonly capped at 10% (5% under certain US–NZ DTA categories), and interest is commonly capped at 10% (certain Australia–NZ interest payments may benefit from a 0% rate where connected to an Australian PE of the NZ borrower). Royalty and interest payments from an EOR entity to an offshore parent must be supported by arm's-length transfer pricing documentation and valid TRCs; mischaracterised management or service fees may be recharacterised as dividends and assessed at the dividend rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand has no single bright-line mandatory Local File threshold, but the Inland Revenue's transfer pricing guidelines require contemporaneous documentation where related-party cross-border transactions aggregate above NZD 1 million for non-financial transactions and NZD 100,000 for related-party loans and financial arrangements. MNE groups with consolidated annual group revenue of NZD 1.14 billion (EUR 750 million) or more must file Country-by-Country Reports with the IRD and retain a Master File. EOR platforms should nonetheless prepare full Local File documentation for all intercompany payroll service fees, software royalties, and management charges, as the IRD applies a risk-based approach.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not maintain separate Economic Substance Regulations of the Cayman/BVI type. However, the Inland Revenue applies the general anti-avoidance rule (ITA 2007 s BG 1), source and permanent establishment principles, and the transfer pricing reconstruction rules (ITA 2007 subpart GC) to disregard shell companies lacking commercial substance. For a global EOR entity, substance is demonstrated by a local board, employment contracts with local staff, operational payroll systems, invoicing functions, risk assumption, and physical premises. A company with no employees, no office, and no payroll function used solely to route contract income to a foreign principal will be treated as a conduit, its profits reconstructed, and penalties applied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate suppression of EOR service revenue; false payroll records; fabrication of subcontracted contractor costs; knowingly filing an IR4 that materially understates taxable income; use of secret offshore bank accounts to divert fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty of 150% of the evaded tax (Tax Administration Act 1994 s 141E). Criminal conviction under Tax Administration Act 1994 s 143B carries a maximum fine of NZD 150,000 and/or imprisonment of up to 15 years. Forfeiture orders apply under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are liable as principals or parties to the evasion; the corporate veil is pierced under Companies Act 1994 s 15. Civil restitution orders, restraint and freezing orders, travel bans, and extradition arrest warrants are available against directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing EOR margins to a related offshore entity that performs no functions, owns no assets, and bears no risk; charging excessive intercompany management fees or royalties to the offshore parent without arm's-length benchmarking; undocumented intercompany loans at non-commercial rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxable income reconstruction under Income Tax Act 2007 s GC 13. Shortfall penalties: 20% for an unacceptable tax position, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Use-of-money interest runs from the original tax due date.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute or approve non-arm's-length intercompany agreements are personally exposed; TAA 1994 s 86 permits the IRD to recover unpaid company tax from directors; reckless trading claims under Companies Act 1994 ss 135–136 may lead to civil restitution and disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Deduct PAYE / KiwiSaver / ESCT
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as an Employer of Record without registering as an employer; failing to withhold PAYE, ESCT, and KiwiSaver deductions from wages; misclassifying employees as independent contractors to shift tax obligations; paying salary offshore without NZ PAYE treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unremitted PAYE plus late payment penalties (1% immediately, 4% after 7 days, then 1% monthly) and use-of-money interest. Criminal prosecution under TAA 1994 s 143 can result in fines of up to NZD 50,000; evasion penalties of 150% apply where there is deliberate non-deduction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: TAA 1994 s 86 imposes personal liability on directors of companies that fail to pay PAYE, KiwiSaver, and GST within 30 days of IRD demand. Directors may face bankruptcy proceedings, asset seizure, and departure prohibition orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Resident Withholding Tax Avoidance on Dividend Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends or deemed dividends to the offshore shareholder without deducting 30% NRWT while lacking a valid TRC or DTA reduced-rate approval; disguising dividends as loans, management fees, or untaxed intercompany charges to avoid withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The full NRWT amount is recoverable from the New Zealand company, plus late payment penalties and interest. Shortfall penalties up to 150% apply where the non-withholding was deliberate. The IRD may recharacterise the payment under s BG 1 and impose an additional 100% penalty for an abusive tax position.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under TAA 1994 s 86, directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid NRWT when the company defaults. Personal assessment, registration of civil judgments against directors, travel restrictions, and contempt-of-court sanctions are enforceable in NZ courts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Violations and Shell Company Utilisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the NZ EOR entity as a conduit to launder payroll funds through multiple foreign bank accounts; failing to conduct beneficial-ownership or sanctions screening on client contractors; creating a façade company with no substance solely to obtain treaty benefits or evade foreign tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil pecuniary penalties under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 of up to NZD 2 million per contravention for companies; criminal fines of up to NZD 100,000 and imprisonment of up to 2 years for officers. The Companies Act 1994 permits shareholder filing; IRD can apply for deregistration for persistent non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior managers and directors are exposed to personal prosecution, property forfeiture under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009, director disqualification under Companies Act 1994 s 383, and cross-border arrest through mutual assistance treaties.
